metadata.name: lspci
metadata.description: List PCI buses and connected devices

installation.note: lspci is commonly available by default; if missing: sudo apt install pciutils

overview.summary: lspci lists PCI (and often PCIe) devices: graphics cards, network adapters, storage controllers, etc. It shows vendor and device IDs and optional human-readable names, useful for identifying hardware and drivers.
when_to_use: See what PCI/PCIe devices are in the system
Identify graphics, network, or storage controllers
Find vendor/device IDs for driver or compatibility checks

syntax.description: lspci reads from /sys and (with root) can query PCI config space. Options control verbosity and output.

options.description: Show detailed information for each device
Show both numeric IDs and names (vendor:device)
options.use_case: Identify hardware by ID for drivers

options.description: Show kernel drivers in use for each device
options.use_case: See which driver is bound to each device

examples.title: List PCI devices
examples.description: Show all PCI/PCIe devices with short descriptions
examples.output:
00:00.0 Host bridge: Intel Corp. ...
01:00.0 VGA compatible controller: ...

examples.title: Show kernel drivers
examples.description: List devices and the kernel driver in use
